manuscript_prose.section1_title: Evolutionary Origins and Biosecurity Risk of Invasive Gastropods in Australia and New Zealand
manuscript_prose.section1_p1: Biological invasions by marine, freshwater, and terrestrial gastropods across Australia and New Zealand span independently introduced lineages ranging from ballast-borne muricids and amphibious Pomacea apple snails to clonal Potamopyrgus mud snails and Mediterranean crop-pest helicids (Theba pisana, Cornu aspersum, Cernuella virgata, Cochlicella spp.).
manuscript_prose.section1_p2: In v2.0.0, all 64 stratified Gastropoda slots ([A]-[G]) execute end-to-end through the generalized declarative bio-suite-supervisor engine with Partitioned ModelTest, empirical Kishino-Hasegawa Z-scores, empirical TimeTreeLSD2 asymmetric HPDs, homogeneous Code-1 GH9, Hsp70, CA2, and CYP3A43 selection models, and 12 real single-species Bayesian skylines.
manuscript_prose.section2_title: Sixteen-Locus Partitioned ModelTest, RY3 De-Biasing & Cambrian-to-Oligocene Gastropod Chronogram
manuscript_prose.section4_title: Purifying Constraint on GH9/GH45 Cellulases, Aestivation Hsp70, Shell CA & CYP3A P450s (1TQN)
manuscript_prose.section4_body: Across 48 verified Universal Code 1 molluscan coding orthologs, Goldman-Yang 61-state codon models quantify constraint on digestive GH9 cellulases (FAM-01), aestivation Hsp70 chaperones (FAM-02), mantle carbonic anhydrases (FAM-03), and microsomal detoxification CYP3A43 monooxygenases (FAM-04) threaded onto PDB 1TQN (2.05 A).
manuscript_prose.section5_title: Conspecific Invasion Skylines (Lissachatina, Helicidae, Potamopyrgus & Pomacea) & Haplotype Networks
discussion_paragraphs: **Deep Divergent Pathways to Terrestrial and Freshwater Invasiveness.** De-biasing pulmonate and caenogastropod compositional skew via partitioned RY3 inference (RCFV = 0.0064; Δln L = +5,211.5) underscores that Australasia's highest-priority invasive snails belong to two clades separated since the Late Devonian (~363.6 Ma): operculate, gill- or lung-bearing Caenogastropoda (*Pomacea*, *Potamopyrgus*) and air-breathing Stylommatophora (*Lissachatina*, *Cornu*, *Theba*, *Cernuella*, *Cochlicella*) [2–4, 7]. Within Helicoidea, our Oligocene divergence estimate (~26.0 Ma) between Helicidae (*Cornu*, *Theba*) and Geomitridae (*Cernuella*, *Cochlicella*) explains why summer stalk-climbing aestivation and calcareous epiphragm sealing represent shared, pre-adapted Circum-Mediterranean dryland syndromes that allowed four distinct species to co-invade southern Australian calcareous mallee and Yorke Peninsula grainlands [4–6, 14].

**Contrasting Invasion Genetics: Serial Clonal/Founder Bottlenecks Versus Multi-Wave Admixture.** Comparing conspecific skylines and *COX1* networks across all 12 pest cohorts reveals why management outcomes differ sharply across invasive mollusks. *Lissachatina fulica* exhibits extreme mitochondrial homogeneity (π = 0.0020, *D* = −2.61, dominated by hub haplotype H01) tracing to documented 19th- and 20th-century stepping-stone introductions from East Africa through Mauritius, India, and Southeast Asia into the Pacific [13]. Similarly, invasive *Potamopyrgus antipodarum* clones outside New Zealand derive from a tiny subset of native-range triploid parthenogenetic lineages [11, 12]. By contrast, *Cornu aspersum*, *Theba pisana*, *Cernuella virgata*, and *Pomacea canaliculata* harbor high standing diversity (*D* = +0.18 to +1.98) seeded by repeated maritime ballast, forage, and aquarium introductions from structured native ranges [5, 8, 14].

**Physiological Pre-Adaptation and Molluscicide Detoxification Constraints.** Chromosome-level gastropod genomes (*Pomacea canaliculata* [10] and *Lissachatina fulica* [13]) have highlighted expanded chaperones, cellulases, and cytochrome P450 repertoires in invasive snails. Our Goldman–Yang codon analysis [17] shows that individual orthologous copies of *Hsp70* (dN/dS = 0.124; 95.8% of codons at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.089) and *GH9/GH45* cellulases (dN/dS = 0.153) remain under tight purifying selection, preserving protein-folding stability when internal shell temperatures exceed 45 °C on sun-exposed cereal stubble [6, 14]. Meanwhile, conservation of the 865 Å<sup>3</sup> *CYP3A* heme pocket (PDB 1TQN; TM-score = 1.000) alongside elevated peripheral loop tolerance (M0 dN/dS = 0.394) supports metabolic detoxification of methiocarb and metaldehyde baits.

**Implications for Biological Control and Quarantine Diagnostics.** High intraspecific diversity within Australian-established *Cernuella virgata* and *Cochlicella acuta* underscores the importance of host-biotype matching when deploying European sarcophagid parasitoid flies (*Sarcophaga villeneuveana*) for classical biological control [6, 14], while the 40-cluster freshwater/achatinid *COX1* reference network (**Figure 7B**) enables rapid distinction between regulated *Pomacea canaliculata* and *P. maculata* egg-mass intercepts [8].

**Study Limitations.** Two limitations bound this study. First, complete mitogenomes and nuclear coding transcriptomes remain unevenly sampled among Geomitridae (*Cochlicella*, *Prietocella*) and endemic Australasian camaenids/charopids, restricting ≥80% supermatrix concatenation to 47 species while integrating the remaining 17 species via quartet coalescent and barcode modules. Second, *COX1* barcodes track maternal ancestry and should be paired with nuclear microsatellites or RAD-seq when testing post-introduction hybridization between *Pomacea canaliculata* and *P. maculata* [8, 9].
manuscript_prose.abstract_context: Understanding how invasive marine, freshwater, and terrestrial snails establish across Australia and New Zealand requires resolving deep gastropod relationships alongside stress-tolerance selection and introduction bottlenecks.
manuscript_prose.executive_summary_lead: traces invasion phylogenomics, aestivation selection, and demography of Australasian snails
manuscript_prose.latex_intro: Sixty-four Gastropoda lineages spanning Patellogastropoda outgroups [A] through Helicoidea crop pests [G] are evaluated across 16 loci in Version 2.0.0.
manuscript_prose.abstract_override: Invasive terrestrial and freshwater gastropods pose severe agricultural, pastoral, and freshwater biosecurity threats across Australia and New Zealand—fouling export cereal harvests, devouring pasture legumes, vectoring zoonotic nematodes, and displacing endemic island malacofaunas. Yet biosecurity risk frameworks rarely integrate deep Paleozoic–Cenozoic gastropod phylogenomics with aestivation, shell-calcification, and molluscicide-detoxification constraints. Here, we analyze a 15-locus mitochondrial and nuclear ribosomal/coding supermatrix (12,753 aligned base pairs; 8,550 parsimony-informative sites) across 64 gastropod species spanning Patellogastropoda/Vetigastropoda outgroups, freshwater invasive Caenogastropoda (Pomacea canaliculata, P. maculata, Potamopyrgus antipodarum), Hygrophila vector snails, tropical Achatinidae (Lissachatina fulica), Asian Bradybaeninae, and Mediterranean grain-fouling Helicidae and Geomitridae (Cornu aspersum, Theba pisana, Cernuella virgata, Cochlicella acuta). Partitioned BIC model selection and third-codon RY3 recoding reduced compositional heterogeneity by 90.3% (RCFV = 0.0064 vs. 0.0661 unrecoded and 0.1617 unfiltered; Δln L = +5,211.49), achieving 96.1% mean bootstrap support across 47 completeness-gated taxa and Q = 0.9038 quartet concordance across all 64 species (6,164,392 / 6,820,300 quartets). Relaxed-clock dating places crown Gastropoda in the Late Cambrian at 497.3 Ma (95% HPD: 470.0–524.7 Ma), the Caenogastropoda–Heterobranchia split at 363.6 Ma (343.6–383.6 Ma), crown Panpulmonata at 177.8 Ma (165.2–187.5 Ma), Stylommatophora at 96.6 Ma (88.0–103.4 Ma), and Mediterranean Helicidae–Geomitridae pest divergence in the Oligocene at 26.0 Ma (24.6–29.2 Ma). Codon models across 39 deduplicated orthologs of GH9/GH45 cellulases, Hsp70, CA2/CA15, and CYP3A confirm purifying selection (dN/dS = 0.124–0.394; zero BEB sites) and conserved 1TQN P450 pocket geometry (TM-score = 1.000).
section1_paragraphs: Australia and New Zealand harbor highly endemic terrestrial and freshwater mollusk assemblages while confronting recurrent biological invasions by Palearctic, Neotropical, and Afrotropical pest gastropods [6–8, 12, 14]. Across southern Australian winter-rainfall grain belts (South Australia, Victoria, and Western Australia), introduced Mediterranean land snails of families Helicidae and Geomitridae—specifically the white Italian snail (*Theba pisana*), vineyard snail (*Cernuella virgata*), pointed snail (*Cochlicella acuta*), and brown garden snail (*Cornu aspersum*)—climb cereal stalks to aestivate during summer heat, clogging combine harvesters and contaminating export wheat and barley shipments above zero-tolerance phytosanitary thresholds [5–7, 14]. Concurrently, Australasian border agencies maintain continuous quarantine vigilance against the giant African land snail (*Lissachatina fulica*), a polyphagous crop pest and rat-lungworm (*Angiostrongylus cantonensis*) vector [13], and against Neotropical golden apple snails (*Pomacea canaliculata* and *P. maculata*) threatening northern wetlands and rice agroecosystems [8–10], while New Zealand's native mud snail (*Potamopyrgus antipodarum*) has itself become a globally invasive parthenogenetic colonist across Australian, European, and North American watersheds [11, 12].

Linking these ecologically diverse invaders within a single evolutionary and physiological framework requires spanning nearly 500 million years of gastropod evolution across Caenogastropoda and Heterobranchia (Panpulmonata) [2–4]. Deep gastropod mitogenomics is notoriously challenged by accelerated substitution rates and strand-asymmetric base composition within pulmonate heterobranchs, which historically destabilized Apogastropoda rooting under unpartitioned nucleotide models [2, 3]. At the organismal level, invasive success across arid Mediterranean pastures and seasonal wetlands depends on a shared suite of physiological pre-adaptations: endogenous digestive cellulases (*GH9/GH45*), summer-aestivation molecular chaperones (*Hsp70*), mantle carbonic anhydrases (*CA2/CA15*) that rapidly calcify shells and sealing epiphragms, and microsomal *CYP3A* monooxygenases that metabolize plant alkaloids and carbamate/metaldehyde molluscicide baits [9, 10, 13, 14].

Here, we analyze 459 curated gastropod sequence records across 64 species (quarantining 1,913 chimeric, misidentified, or frameshifted submissions) spanning 16 mitochondrial and nuclear rDNA/coding partitions [1–4]. We combine edge-linked per-locus BIC model selection and third-codon RY3 recoding with fossil-calibrated relaxed-clock dating [2–4], 64-species quartet multispecies coalescent inference [15], and four-taxon Patterson's *D* tests, paired with 61-state Goldman–Yang codon selection [17] across *GH9/GH45* cellulases, *Hsp70*, *CA2/CA15*, and *CYP3A* monooxygenases threaded onto PDB 1TQN, plus 12 strictly conspecific coalescent skylines and *COX1* biosecurity networks [5, 8, 11–14, 16].
section2_paragraphs: Automated homology curation and reading-frame validation across all 64 gastropod taxa yielded a 15-partition supermatrix of 12,753 aligned base pairs containing 8,550 parsimony-informative RY3 sites [1–3]. Per-locus BIC model selection with proportional partition rate multipliers and third-codon RY3 recoding reduced relative composition frequency variability by 90.3%—from RCFV = 0.0661 under unrecoded four-state nucleotides and 0.1617 in unfiltered controls to RCFV = 0.0064—and improved marginal log-likelihood by Δln L = +5,211.49 units (ln L = −255,335.49 vs. −260,546.98 unpartitioned; ΔBIC = −9,061.7) across 47 completeness-gated species with disambiguated geographic mitogenome slots (**Figures 1 & 2**; **Tables 3A, 3C & 3D**). Mean ultrafast bootstrap support rose from 87.2% in single-locus barcodes to 96.1% under partitioned RY3 inference.

Rooted on Patellogastropoda and Vetigastropoda outgroups ([A]), the partitioned timetree recovers Apogastropoda uniting Caenogastropoda ([B]–[D]) and Heterobranchia/Panpulmonata ([E]–[G], 100% UFBoot2), concordant with phylotranscriptomic gastropod syntheses [2, 3]. Constrained relaxed-clock dating places the crown Gastropoda root (**Node I**) in the Furongian Late Cambrian at 497.3 Ma (95% HPD: 470.0–524.7 Ma) and the Caenogastropoda–Heterobranchia split (**Node II**) in the Famennian Late Devonian at 363.6 Ma (343.6–383.6 Ma) [2, 3]. Within Caenogastropoda, Architaenioglossa apple snails ([C], *Pomacea*) diverge from Littorinimorpha/Neogastropoda in the Middle Triassic (**Node III**: 243.8 Ma; 224.3–257.2 Ma), and Tateidae mud snails (*Potamopyrgus antipodarum*) split from pomatiopsid/assimineid truncatelloideans in the Late Jurassic (**Node IV**: 153.0 Ma; 144.6–164.2 Ma). Parallel diversification in Panpulmonata separates freshwater Hygrophila ([E]) from terrestrial Stylommatophora in the Early Jurassic (**Node V**: 177.8 Ma; 165.2–187.5 Ma), basal achatinoid *Lissachatina fulica* from non-achatinoid Sigmurethra in the Cenomanian Late Cretaceous (**Node VI**: 96.6 Ma; 88.0–103.4 Ma) [4, 13], Asian Camaenidae/Bradybaeninae ([F]) from Palearctic Helicoidea in the Middle Eocene (**Node VII**: 45.6 Ma; 41.7–50.8 Ma), and Mediterranean Helicidae (*Cornu aspersum*, *Theba pisana*) from Geomitridae (*Cernuella virgata*, *Cochlicella acuta*) in the Chattian Oligocene (**Node VIII**: 26.0 Ma; 24.6–29.2 Ma; **Figure 1**; **Table 2A**) [4–6, 14].
section3_paragraphs: Reconciling individual gene trees across all 64 gastropod species—including regional Australasian pasture pests and quarantine-intercepted taxa below the 80% supermatrix completeness threshold—under the 16-locus quartet multispecies coalescent [1, 15] satisfied 6,164,392 of 6,820,300 evaluated four-taxon quartets, yielding normalized concordance Q = 0.9038 and mean local posterior probability LPP = 0.8622 (**Figure 3**; **Figure 6**; **Table 3A**). Quartet concordance reaches 1.000 on Caenogastropoda (**Node III**, LPP = 1.00) and strongly supports Truncatelloidea/Tateidae (**Node IV**, q1 = 0.736, LPP = 0.99; **Table 2A & 2B**) [2–4].

Four-taxon Patterson's *D* tests (**Table 2B**) show symmetrical background allele sorting without cross-genus introgression across Mediterranean Helicidae (*Cornu aspersum* / *Cantareus apertus* vs. *Helix pomatia*, ABBA-1: *D* = −0.0807, *Z* = 1.70) [5], Geomitridae dune snails (*Cernuella virgata* / *Helicella itala* vs. *Monacha cartusiana*, ABBA-2: *D* = −0.0680, *Z* = 1.19) [4, 14], invasive *Pomacea maculata* and *P. canaliculata* (ABBA-3: *D* = −0.0800, *Z* = 1.13) [8], and *Potamopyrgus antipodarum* / *P. estuarinus* (ABBA-4: *D* = −0.0714, *Z* = 1.00) [11].
section4_paragraphs: Fitting 61-state Goldman–Yang codon substitution models [17] across 39 species-deduplicated gastropod coding orthologs aligned under 20-state BLOSUM62 L-INS-i consistency demonstrates net purifying selection across all four physiological gene families (BEB Pr ≥ 0.95 = 0 sites across all families; **Figure 5A–B**; **Table 4A**). Summer-aestivation molecular chaperone *Hsp70* experiences the tightest constraint (FAM-02; N = 11 species, 637 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1237, κ = 1.31; 95.8% of sites at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.0894), followed by endogenous digestive endo-β-1,4-glucanases *GH9/GH45* that hydrolyze pasture and macrophyte cellulose (FAM-01; N = 12 species, 579 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1528, κ = 1.27; 68.6% of sites at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.1170) [9, 10, 13]. Mantle carbonic anhydrases *CA2/CA15* mediating rapid CaCO<sub>3</sub> shell repair and calcified epiphragm sealing (FAM-03; N = 9 species, 310 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.2616, κ = 1.18) and xenobiotic/molluscicide-metabolizing *CYP3A* monooxygenases (FAM-04; N = 7 species, 492 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.3942, κ = 1.41; 56.3% of sites at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.1514) exhibit conserved catalytic cores flanked by more permissive surface loops [10, 13].

Three-dimensional threading of gastropod *CYP3A* onto the 2.05 Å crystal structure of microsomal CYP3A4 (PDB 1TQN Chain A with protoporphyrin IX HEM A 508 and proximal Cys442 Sγ coordination) confirms complete structural conservation of the P450 fold (TM-score = 1.0000) enclosing an 865.0 Å<sup>3</sup> catalytic pocket (estimated affinity −12.36 kcal/mol; **Figure 5D**), supporting oxidative clearance of dietary phytotoxins and carbamate/metaldehyde baits [10, 13].
section5_paragraphs: Twelve strictly conspecific Bayesian coalescent skylines (25,000 MCMC generations, 20% burn-in) reveal stark demographic contrasts between multi-source Mediterranean pasture introductions and severe single-founder tropical bottlenecks (**Figures 4A & 4B**; **Table 4B**) [1, 16]. Giant African land snail *Lissachatina fulica* displays ultra-low mitochondrial diversity and strongly negative Tajima's *D* (R6, N = 36, π = 0.0020, *D* = −2.61), capturing the classic serial founder bottleneck of the pantropical Indo-Pacific invasion lineage [13], mirrored in miniature by horticultural tramp snail *Bradybaena similaris* (R5, N = 35, π = 0.0311, *D* = −1.08). Conversely, Mediterranean helicid and geomitrid snails—*Theba pisana* (R1, N = 36, π = 0.0787, *D* = +0.91; nuclear L3 π = 0.0531), *Cornu aspersum* (R2, N = 31, π = 0.0741, *D* = +0.18; nuclear ITS/28S L2 π = 0.0543) [5], *Cernuella virgata* (R3, N = 36, π = 0.0728, *D* = +1.98), and *Cochlicella acuta* (R4, N = 25, π = 0.0603, *D* = +1.53) [6, 14]—retain deep Western Palearctic sub-lineage diversity across multiple historical introduction waves, paralleled by multiple South American source clades in *Pomacea canaliculata* (L4 *COX1* π = 0.0306, *D* = +1.24 vs. L5 ITS rDNA *D* = −0.89 and L6 coding *D* = −2.01) [8] and mixed sexual/clonal lineages in New Zealand *Potamopyrgus antipodarum* (L1, N = 31, π = 0.0165, *D* = +0.74) [11, 12].

Minimum-spanning and TCS *COX1* haplotype networks (**Figures 7A & 7B**; **Table 4C**) partition 137 Mediterranean and Australasian Helicidae/Geomitridae sequences into 76 clusters (Panel A, 110 haplotypes across 636 bp, *H*<sub>d</sub> = 0.9954) and 134 freshwater/tropical apple, mud, and achatinid snail sequences into 40 clusters (Panel B, 83 haplotypes across 642 bp, *H*<sub>d</sub> = 0.9767), dominated by a central 18-isolate *Lissachatina fulica* pantropical invasion hub (H01; **Table 4C**).
manuscript_prose.section6_intro: Complete sequence-hygiene logs, Cambrian–Oligocene relaxed-clock calibrations, clade benchmark and ABBA–BABA statistics, 32-chain model selection rankings, per-locus BIC rate multipliers, Goldman–Yang codon selection summaries, and conspecific coalescent skyline metrics are compiled in **Tables 1–4C** below [1, 15–17].
